in_english.name: Israheel
in_english.long_meaning: Israheel is a masculine given name derived from Arabic roots. It means 'God will rule' or 'God's servant', and is associated with the biblical figure Jacob, who is referred to as Israheel in the Quran. The name holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition, reflecting the themes of divine guidance and servitude.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Israheel" is derived from the Arabic root 'srh', meaning 'to guide, to follow a certain path, or to direct'. In Islamic tradition, the name "Israfil" is deeply connected to the prophecy of the Trumpet Blast at the End of Days. Israfil (Israel in some translations) holds immense significance in Middle Eastern folklore as well, and the name is often used for sons to impart a hopeful and blessed meaning. Beyond its usage in proper names, the term also finds mention in several Sufi poems, songs, and stories.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name "Israheel" signifies the divine guidance that God bestows upon His servants. In the Quran (76:1-5), we are told that on the Day of Resurrection, God will call out, "Israfil, son of Absal! Strike! And whoever is within the Mega qara (dense forest) [of sins] and within the Ard-Ard (wide plain) [of goodness], will be blown towards it [i.e., towards God]." Here, the name signifies God's call for accountability and the subsequent separation of the righteous from the wicked. It is a poignant reminder that whatever path we follow in life, the ultimate guidance comes from our Creator, and our spiritual destiny is in His hands.
